items.title: Eddie Summers Interview, 1960-09-16
items.q: That was the later group. That was the later group. It was Claiborne Williams and LeBlanc... They didn't play in that band.

ctx.x: And he had a daughter played piano named Mary, Mary Williams. Oh. But that's after his time. That wasn't in his time. That's his children.

There was one famous trombonist by the name of Williams. I never could find out if he's related. One of the brothers of Claiborne or son too. Is it Williamton? I can't think of his first name now. I know Roy Palmer told me about him, that he was inspired by him. And he traveled with Handy for a while. Johnny Handy? No, no. With W.C. Handy, the St. Louis Blues composer. Oh, St. Louis Blues, I see. He went up to Memphis. I'm not sure he was one of that family, but I always wondered. Well, I wouldn't know him. You…
